h: Tinopolis, Amelia Earhart and Kidwelly's Castle
p: Keep an eye on the sky over the Burry Inlet, as the estuary is a magnet for wading birds such as curlews and oystercatchers, with winter bringing the biggest numbers. Watching a flock of waders twist and turn over the mudflats as the tide comes in is pure magic, so a tide table is your friend.
A picnic with a view across to the Gower is the perfect way to round it off.

Llanelli has a proud industrial history. It was once known as Tinopolis because of its huge tinplate industry, and the town's rugby anthem, Sosban Fach, which means little saucepan, is a nod to that heritage. You'll see saucepans on top of the rugby posts at Parc y Scarlets, home of the Scarlets.

Just along the coast at Burry Port, a memorial marks the spot where Amelia Earhart landed in 1928, becoming the first woman to fly across the Atlantic as a passenger. The harbour is a lovely spot for a stroll. A short drive further west, Kidwelly Castle is a well-preserved medieval fortress beside the River Gwendraeth, perfect for exploring with kids who love towers and battlements.

Rugby fans will know that Llanelli has a special place in the game's history. In 1972, Llanelli famously beat the touring All Blacks 9-3 at the old Stradey Park ground, a victory still celebrated in the town. For a quieter cultural stop, Parc Howard Museum is set in a Victorian mansion surrounded by parkland and has a collection of Llanelli pottery and local history, plus a park with a play area and gardens. And when you're looking out across the estuary from the wetland centre, keep an eye out for Whiteford Lighthouse, a cast-iron tower standing in the water off the north coast of Gower.
